definition: TODO: A set of vertices joined by edges; positions and edge lengths in the drawing don't matter, only the connections
TODO: A point of a graph (also called a node), joined to others by edges
TODO: A line joining two vertices of a graph (or one vertex to itself for a loop)
TODO: The number of edge ends at a vertex; a loop counts twice; the degrees add up to twice the number of edges
TODO: A graph with no loops and no multiple edges between the same pair of vertices
TODO: A simple graph with every pair of vertices joined by exactly one edge; K_n has n(n − 1)/2 edges
TODO: A graph with a number (weight) on each edge, such as a cost, distance or time
TODO: A graph with a path between every pair of vertices
TODO: A directed graph in which every vertex can be reached from every other vertex following the edge directions
TODO: A graph whose edges have directions (arrows) and can be travelled only one way; a vertex's in-degree counts edges coming in, its out-degree edges going out
TODO: A graph made from some of the vertices and edges of another graph, where every chosen edge keeps both its end vertices
TODO: A connected graph with no cycles; a tree with n vertices has n − 1 edges
